summary: Lookout in the top room of the old Mount Tom Hotel, first operated 1914; the summit house burned in 1929 and only a concrete foundation remains, off-limits to the public.

facts.design: Observation room in the top room of the Mount Tom summit hotel, equipped with 18 telescopes
facts.status_note: The summit house burned in May 1929 and the later temporary building was removed; a concrete foundation remains and is off-limits to the public.

access.note: The summit foundation is off-limits to the public; the summit is reached on the New England National Scenic Trail

visit.trail_note: Steep 0.8-mile ascent via the New England National Scenic Trail from the MA 141 trailhead near the Holyoke-Easthampton town line

events.note: Holyoke Street Railway Company built the first of three summit buildings, a two-story pavilion
Fire destroyed the first pavilion in October 1900
Seven-story replacement with observatory and copper dome opened; it stood until 1929
Top room of the old Mount Tom Hotel first operated as a lookout; state given permission to use the observation room
Second summit house burned in May 1929, in part due to water system failures (Wikipedia)
Temporary steel (Estuary) or sheet metal (Wikipedia) building dismantled; Estuary says removed when the park closed in the late 1930s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Estuary Magazine calls the third summit building a temporary steel building; Wikipedia calls the cheaper replacement a sheet metal structure. The story reports both descriptions.

sources.title: Central Watershed Outings: Summit Houses of the Pioneer Valley

notes_for_editor: The register's 'Mount Tom Hotel' is read as the summit house rebuilt in 1901, which stood on the summit until the May 1929 fire. No fetched source ties the 1914 lookout to that building by name, so the story flags it as likely. The FFLA Massachusetts Facebook post on the old summit house (upper room used for fire detection in the 1910s) would not fetch and is not cited. The brief's kind 'unknown' should be 'tower' per the register's 60-foot tower. Last year of lookout operation and staffing were not found. The site has a foundation, not a standing lookout, so status 'gone' matches the sources.
